clauses.reason: The sole operative paragraph of Executive Order 6204-A reads, in its operative part: "I therefore hereby approve of said provisions of said Code for the Rayon Weaving Industry subject to the interpretations and conditions imposed by me on my approval of the corresponding provisions of said Cotton Textile Code and subject further to such revisions or modifications as I may find proper after a hearing has been held on said Code of Fair Competition for the Rayon Weaving Industry, now set for July 25, 1933". It approves only the provisions of Section V, paragraphs (a), (b), (d) and (e) of the Rayon Weaving code, to be effective on July 17, 1933, subject to the conditions imposed on the corresponding Cotton Textile Code provisions and to such revisions or modifications as the President may find proper after a hearing. The reservation of a power to revise after a hearing set for July 25, 1933 states no period or end: it is a power, and no held record shows that it was exercised. The hearing date is a scheduled event, not an end of the approval. The conditions imported from the Cotton Textile approval are incorporated as they stood and add no end of their own. The approval was code-dependent: under section 3(b) of the Act the approved provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under section 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under section 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor, so the approval operated only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval, so the approval ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended or superseded (for example by a full approval of the Rayon Weaving code) before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end date: section 1 of the same resolution replaced the original two-year expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not as an end date.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6204-A (July 14, 1933) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Rayon Weaving Industry (provisions of Section V, paragraphs (a), (b), (d) and (e), approved immediately) under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; Common Crawl capture 2025-11-17T01:15:37Z); the standing note applies: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order is a partial approval made effective July 17, 1933, with a reserved power to revise after a hearing. Because each command is dependent on the code and no held record shows an earlier end, the first end is the statutory repeal of the code approval and enforcement provisions by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, effective June 14, 1935. Schechter, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; that is recorded as a validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no approval. The antitrust-exemption proviso of the resolution is not settled by the held text for past action; whatever survives is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.

Res. 113 or in any held source continues the approval or its enforcement after June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution or injunction continued under this approval after that date.
